explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/386: this variant takes the reading in which k is fixed. For every k ≥ 2, is C(n,k) a product of consecutive primes for infinitely many n? Erdős–Graham expected this never happens for 3 ≤ k ≤ n-3, so the variant is probably false, but it is a legitimate open reading of the question and is stated correctly. Faithful.
